counterexample: The 5f380 StateEquilibrator branches mutate only the water source phase, then globally remove every water portion at or below 1e-12 mol. A distinct 5e-13 mol gas-water portion therefore vanishes without an event during freezing, melting, or boiling in the current source. The successor predicate prunes liquid water for freezing/boiling and solid water for melting, retaining the gas portion byte-exact. The control requires the typed water transition and exact retained gas Portion in each branch.

design_limits: The gas-water trace in an open vessel is a source bookkeeping probe, not a claim that open-vessel water vapor is a stable equilibrium state. It is deliberately outside the liquid/ice transfer ownership of these State branches.

A tiny solid-water trace cannot exercise the boiling branch at 400 K: source branch order first selects melting whenever frozen_water && now > freezing_k. Gas-water is the available untouched water phase for an exact boiling control.

The control does not cover destination-phase water traces merged by deposit; such a control would need event-adjusted total-phase accounting and an explicit floating-arithmetic bound. The existing unrelated 5e-13 mol NaCl control remains in source.
The patch changes no raw 1e-12 transfer floor, 32-pass bound, joint certificate budget, native adapter, physical model, or acceptance threshold.
